facts.text: Geralt of Rivia was born to Vizenna, a sorceress and druid who was a rare woman able to conceive despite practicing magic.
Vizenna abandoned infant Geralt at the gates of Kaer Morhen, giving him to the witchers of the Wolf School.
Geralt grew up knowing his mother was alive, which fostered lasting cynicism toward mages and destiny.
Vesemir, the Wolf School's master at arms, became Geralt's primary father figure and mentor.
Geralt's biological father is rumored in the lore to be a warrior named Corin, though this is never confirmed and Geralt does not dwell on it.
Geralt eventually met Vizenna as an adult, and the reunion was cold and distant rather than warm.
The Trial of the Grasses is a brutal alchemical process meant to mutate child recruits into witchers, killing most who undergo it.
Only about three out of every ten children who undergo the Trial of the Grasses at Kaer Morhen survive to become witchers.
Geralt survived the Trial of the Grasses with unusual resilience, leading the mages to subject him to additional experimental mutations.
The extra experimental mutations stripped all pigment from Geralt's body, turning his skin pale and his hair white.
Geralt's white hair and pale skin earned him the nickname Gwynbleidd, meaning White Wolf.
The additional mutations gave Geralt faster reflexes, superior night vision, and an extremely high resistance to toxins compared to standard witchers.
The mutations that created witchers also dampen emotional responses to help them face monsters without fear.
Witcher trainees were encouraged to adopt surnames so they would appear trustworthy to clients rather than seeming like nameless drifters.
As a young man, Geralt originally wanted to name himself Geralt Roger Eric du Haute-Bellegarde.
Vesemir mocked Geralt's elaborate chosen name and warned it would get him killed or mocked on the road.
Geralt settled on the surname 'of Rivia' despite having no actual connection to the kingdom of Rivia.
Geralt practiced a Rivian accent to make his invented identity more convincing.
During the second war with Nilfgaard, Geralt fought at a bridge over the Yaruga River to protect the forces of Queen Meve of Lyria and Rivia.
Queen Meve knighted Geralt for his bravery at the Yaruga River battle, making his invented title 'of Rivia' officially legitimate.

In Blaviken, Geralt was caught between the wizard Stregobor, who believed in a prophecy that girls born during an eclipse become monsters, and Renfri, a cursed princess turned bandit leader Stregobor had long hunted.
Renfri threatened to massacre the market crowd in Blaviken unless Stregobor was forced out of his tower.
Geralt killed Renfri and her gang in the Blaviken market to prevent a larger massacre of townsfolk.
The townsfolk of Blaviken did not know about Renfri's ultimatum and instead saw Geralt as a murderous freak, stoning him and driving him out.
The Blaviken massacre earned Geralt the lasting reputation and title 'Butcher of Blaviken.'
The Blaviken incident made Geralt more reluctant to interfere in human affairs and reinforced his reliance on the Witcher's code as an emotional shield.
The Witcher's Code theoretically requires witchers to remain neutral in human wars, politics, and religious conflicts.
Witcher neutrality was originally meant to keep witcher schools from becoming political targets of kings or religious authorities.
There is no single official written code for witchers; the code is largely an informal professional convention.
Geralt often quotes the line 'If I'm to choose between one evil and another, I'd rather not choose at all,' though he repeatedly fails to remain neutral.
Geralt carries a steel sword for humans and mundane creatures and a silver sword for monsters born of the conjunction of the spheres.
Geralt uses five basic combat Signs: Aard for telekinetic force, Igni for flame, Yrden for magical traps, Quen for a protective shield, and Axii for mind manipulation.
Witcher signs are a weaker form of magic compared to full sorceress spellcasting, but are effective combat tools.
Geralt relies on a heightened sensory ability called Witcher's sense to track scents and hear hidden monsters.
Witchers use alchemical oils on blades and decoctions in their blood to temporarily boost combat abilities, though these are highly toxic even to mutated witcher biology.
Under the effects of strong alchemical potions, a witcher's skin pales further, veins darken, and eyes turn black.
Geralt met Dandelion (Julian Alfred Pancratz) at a talent contest in Goulette, where Geralt ended up protecting him from the brothers of a girl Dandelion had seduced.
Dandelion turned Geralt's grim exploits, including the Blaviken massacre, into romanticized ballads that built Geralt's public legend as the White Wolf.
Dandelion provides Geralt with social connections, gossip, and logistical help that Geralt would otherwise lack living on the road.
Dandelion gave Geralt a home base in the city of Novigrad.
Geralt and Yennefer of Vengerberg first met in the town of Rinde while Geralt sought a cure for a magical ailment afflicting Dandelion.
Yennefer was attempting to capture a djinn in Rinde to restore her fertility and increase her magical power.
Geralt used his third and final wish granted by the djinn to magically bind his fate to Yennefer's, saving her from the creature's retaliation.
The djinn-wish bond between Geralt and Yennefer is later revisited in The Witcher 3, where they attempt to use another djinn to determine if their love is genuine or magically compelled.
Yennefer became a spiritual mother figure to Ciri, deepening her bond with Geralt as they both took on parental roles for her.
Geralt attended a feast in Cintra hosted by Queen Calanthe under the false identity 'Lord of Ravik' to observe political negotiations over Pavetta's marriage.
A knight named Duny, the Urcheon of Erlenwald, arrived at the Cintra feast and claimed Pavetta's hand through the Law of Surprise, having once saved King Roegner's life.
Queen Calanthe intended to have Duny killed to prevent the marriage, but Geralt intervened to protect him.
Geralt used his Witcher signs to help break the curse that kept Duny in a beastial form, restoring his human shape.
When offered a reward, Geralt invoked the Law of Surprise on Duny as a joking gesture, claiming 'that which you already have but do not know.'
At the moment Geralt invoked the Law of Surprise, Pavetta revealed she was already pregnant, meaning Geralt had unknowingly claimed the unborn Ciri as his destiny.
Geralt spent six years trying to avoid the responsibility of his claim on Ciri, taking distant contracts and refusing to return to Cintra.
Ciri is later revealed to carry the Elder Blood, and Geralt's survival and role are tied to his destined connection to her.
